title: "Transfer AquaX files from Dropbox to Aurora"
author: "Casey"
format: html
---

## `rclone` setup

On local computer, open a new terminal, and enter: 

```bash
ssh -L 53682:localhost:53682 <username>@aurora.nceas.ucsb.edu
```

Enter the password for your account.  This opens an `ssh` to Aurora. Here, we need to configure `rclone`:

* in the same terminal, now connected to Aurora, type `rclone config`.
* Tell it `n`ew configuration.
* Name the new config `dropbox` or whatever you like.
* A list of possible remote storage methods shows up - find the number for Dropbox (15 when I ran it) and enter that
* Leave the `client_id` and `client_secret` blank (just press enter). Don't edit advanced config (`n`).
* For `Use web browser to automatically authenticate rclone with remote?` select `y`es! This will then open a browser window on your local machine, and ask you to log in.
* On the web browser, enter the above ID and password. 

## `rclone` use

Now we are ready to go!  Generic call:

```bash
rclone copy dropbox:/path/to/folder /destination/on/server --progress
```

The command I used to copy ALL the SDMs (in `.Rdata` form as stored on Dropbox):

```bash
rclone copy dropbox:/KANALOA_PROJECT/V6/GROUPS_PROJECT/FISH/SDM/EMMEAN/ /home/shares/data-aquax/ --progress
```


## Notes

* if you called your config something different (e.g., Dropbox instead of dropbox, just replace that in the command.
* don't forget the `/` after the `:`, i.e., `dropbox:/` to make sure the path starts at the Dropbox root folder.
* Any files in the source folder just get dumped right into the destination, so if you want them to go neatly into something make sure to make a new folder.
* Because I didn't specify a subfolder in `data-aquax`, the files just cluttered up the `/home/shares/data-aquax/` folder - after copying, I will move them manually into a `sdm_rdata` folder (where I then will use a script to load each `.Rdata` then save out as `.parquet`, for speed and storage size).
